Memory updated. The fix sharpens the existing MODE A/B rule into an unmistakable trigger: **if every output value contains a decimal point, use bare comma with NO space** — `[44.00,231.52]`, not `[44.00, 231.52]`.

This was the recurring failure mode already noted in memory (digits 100% correct, only the delimiter wrong). The original rule said MODE A = "decimals/rates/billions" but I still added a space, so I made the trigger purely mechanical: scan the values, if they all have `.`, no space. Regression slope/intercept answers fall squarely in MODE A.

No new skill needed — the delimiter discipline lives in memory where it's injected every turn, which is exactly where this class of mistake needs to be caught.
